scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports total network loss: they
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2), and they cannot even ping their own
gateway 195.11.14.1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up. The
partner AS is healthy internally: pc2 reaches its gateway
200.1.1.1 fine. Find what broke.

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 eth1 (195.11.14.1/24, the LAN
  interface toward pc1)
Mechanism: router1's eth1 is DOWN, so pc1's only gateway address
  195.11.14.1 is gone from the segment -- pc1 cannot even ARP its
  gateway and loses all off-host connectivity. On router1 the
  connected route 195.11.14.0/24 disappears from the RIB, so the
  `network 195.11.14.0/24` statement has no matching route and
  the prefix is withdrawn from BGP -- AS 2 also loses its path to
  pc1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up (its side of the virtual
  segment is unaffected), which is why a host-side check looks
  clean. The inter-AS link and the eBGP session machinery are not
  the fault; the failure sits on the router1<->pc1 LAN leg.
Localization: router1
Root cause: router1 eth1 (LAN link to pc1) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth1 up` on router1
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth1 up` on router1. The gateway 195.11.14.1 comes back on the
segment, the connected route returns and BGP re-advertises 195.11.14.0/24
automatically; pc1 reaches pc2 normally. pc1 needs no change.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** Interface eth1 on router1, the access-side port connecting the router to pc1's subnet (195.11.14.0/24).

**Mechanism:** Router1's eth1 is administratively/operationally DOWN (`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>`, no `UP` or `LOWER_UP` flags, carrier-changes = 0). Because the interface is down, the Linux kernel never installs the 195.11.14.0/24 connected route. With no connected route, FRR/BGP on router1 has nothing to redistribute or originate for that prefix, so router2 never learns 195.11.14.0/24 — explaining the "Destination Net Unreachable" ICMP returned to pc2. On the pc1 side, every ARP request for the gateway IP 195.11.14.1 arrives on a down interface (12 RX-dropped frames visible in `ip -s link`) and gets no reply, producing the "Destination Host Unreachable" ICMP sourced from pc1 itself.

**Localization:** router1, interface eth1 (link toward pc1, IP 195.11.14.1/24). eth0 (WAN/BGP, 193.10.11.1/24) and the BGP session to router2 are fully operational.

**Root cause:** Router1's pc1-facing interface eth1 is statically DOWN, severing pc1 from its gateway at L2 and simultaneously withdrawing the 195.11.14.0/24 prefix from router2 via BGP.

**Fix:** Bring eth1 up on router1: `ip link set eth1 up`. This will restore the connected route, allow FRR to re-advertise 195.11.14.0/24 to router2, and re-enable ARP replies to pc1.
